question: What does the sibling registry factory dispatch 0x5fd4080 do -- the SystemClock dispatch listed as an open unknown in #4428 -- how does its name lookup 0x5fd3d00 resolve a clock name in the registry, and which code writes a non-kOk Status into the dispatch's 0x30(%rsp) temp (also open in #4428)? Resolves #4428's open unknowns: 'the sibling dispatches at 0x5fd4080..0x5fd4627 and 0x6136b40..0x613721b' (the first of the two) and 'which factory writes a non-kOk Status into the dispatch's 0x30(%rsp) temp'.

open_unknowns: which factory writes a non-kOk Status into the dispatch's 0x30(%rsp) temp (the 0x5ffa2c0 move-assign path in #4428)
resolves.answer: 0x5fd4080 is the SystemClock registry factory dispatch (Status* out, ObjectRegistry* registry, name, shared_ptr<SystemClock>* clock_slot), the same template as #4428's BlockCipher dispatch 0x5ff9fe0 instantiated for the 'SystemClock' factory type. It resolves the name through the lookup 0x5fd3d00, invokes the matched creator through the factory record's +0x18 invoker, and wraps the returned raw object in a fresh 0x18-byte non-inplace shared_ptr control block (vtable 0x64cdf38). No factory writes the 0x30(%rsp) temp: the dispatch itself builds the temp Status in the factory-null branches (0x5fd43d7 when the factory left the string arg empty, 0x5fd441f when it filled it with a message) and in the lookup-miss branch (0x5fd44be), then the shared tail at 0x5fd414b move-assigns it into *out via 0x5fcdf70 at 0x5fd432c -- the same template holds in #4428 (0x5ffa3d9 builds the temp, 0x5ffa0af is the shared tail).

dispatch_0x5fd4080.signature: (Status* out, ObjectRegistry* registry, const std::string& name, shared_ptr<SystemClock>* clock_slot)

outcomes.condition: lookup returns a zeroed record (manager null)
outcomes.note: built into the 0x30(%rsp) temp, then move-assigned into *out by the shared tail at 0x5fd414b

outcomes.condition: factory returns null and left the string arg empty (0x88(%rsp) == 0)
outcomes.note: built into the 0x30(%rsp) temp, then move-assigned into *out by the shared tail at 0x5fd414b

outcomes.condition: factory returns null but filled the string arg with a message (0x88(%rsp) != 0)
outcomes.note: the factory's string is the msg1 string_view (ptr at 0x40(%rsp), size at 0x48(%rsp)); built into the 0x30(%rsp) temp, then move-assigned into *out by the shared tail at 0x5fd414b

outcomes.note: built directly into *out (rdi is rbx); the shared tail is not taken

outcomes.action: new 0x18-byte control block (vtable 0x64cdf38, counts (1,1) from 0x459b20, object at +0x10); store (object, control) into the out clock slot; release the old clock via 0x5d350c0

dispatch_0x5fd4080.record_destroy: after a non-null factory return the record is destroyed via its manager with op 3 (0x5fd4168); a no-op for the stateless creator lambdas, as in #4428
dispatch_0x5fd4080.status_temp: the 16 bytes at 0x30(%rsp) are a Status temp, zeroed to kOk at 0x5fd4133 after the factory call; the dispatch itself writes a non-kOk Status there in the factory-null branches (0x5fd43d7, 0x5fd441f) and the lookup-miss branch (0x5fd44be), and the shared tail at 0x5fd414b move-assigns it into *out via 0x5fcdf70 at 0x5fd432c when its code byte is non-zero. No registered creator writes the temp -- this resolves #4428's open unknown of the same shape (there the temp is built at 0x5ffa3d9 and the shared tail is 0x5ffa0af).
dispatch_0x5fd4080.status_ctor: 0x61cf670(out, code, subcode 0, msg1, msg2, severity 0): msg1 and msg2 are string_views ({ptr, size} pairs at 0x40(%rsp) and 0x50(%rsp)); message is msg1, or msg1 + ': ' + msg2 when msg2 is non-empty

lookup_0x5fd3d00.signature: (FactoryRecord* out, ObjectRegistry* registry, const std::string& name) -> FactoryRecord*

registry_layout.+0x60: parent registry pointer (recursed into on exhaustion)

algorithm: lock the registry mutex at +0x98 (lock failure throws system_error with the errno)
walk the libraries vector backwards, 16-byte elements (first qword = library pointer; second qword unread, open unknown)
per library lock its mutex at +0x00, then query its map at +0x28 for the type name via 0x5fd2980
on a hit walk the entry's candidate vector (+0x28/+0x30) and call each candidate's vtable slot 2 (Matches, forwards to PatternEntry Matches 0x61f8670) with (candidate, name)
on a match clone the factory record (manager op 2, a no-op here, plus the explicit 16-byte copy of the {manager, invoker} pair) into *out and return
on exhaustion unlock and recurse into the parent registry at +0x60; with no parent zero *out
lookup_0x5fd3d00.map_key: SystemClock (11 chars, built SSO: movabs 'SystemCl' at 0x5fd3da5 + 'lock' 0x6b636f6c at 0x5fd3dc1)
lookup_0x5fd3d00.manager_ops_observed: op 2 (clone) at 0x5fd3e68 and op 3 (destroy) at 0x5fd3f78 are called on the record's manager; both are no-ops for the stateless creator lambdas, as in #4428

layout.+0x00: functor storage (16 bytes, zero for stateless lambdas)

factory_record.invoker_signature: (record, name, slot_ptr_ptr, string*) -> raw SystemClock* or null; stores the new raw object at *slot_ptr_ptr; may fill the string arg with an error message when returning null
factory_record.factory_slot_protocol: the creator stores the new raw object pointer at the slot (0x28(%rsp) in the dispatch), destroying any previous object there through its vtable slot 1, and returns the same pointer; null return means failure

control_block.vtable_length_note: exactly 5 function slots. Unlike the BlockCipher control-block vtable 0x64d0198 (#4428), which has a trailing zero slot, the qword after slot 4 here is a RELATIVE reloc to the 'DEBUG' string table at 0x446560 -- the next .data.rel.ro object, not part of this vtable.

dispatcher_and_wrapper.dispatcher_note: mirrors #4402's dispatcher 0x5ffa710: pthread_once init, the options-map host call, the dispatch call, and the configure call. Its internals are cited, not pinned here.
dispatcher_and_wrapper.wrapper_gate: if rcx+0x08 == 2 and the string at (%rcx) starts with 'id' (0x6469) and r8+0x08 == 0, it zeroes the shared_ptr at (%r9) (releasing the old clock via 0x5d350c0) and returns kOk; otherwise it forwards to the dispatcher at 0x5fd4c60
